decisions.why: *velle in* is the Greek's θέλειν ἐν (θελήσει σφόδρα), a Hebraism for delighting in something; DRB 'shall delight exceedingly'. The glossary keeps *velle → querer* (36:23 *et viam ejus volet → e ele quererá o seu caminho*), and Portuguese *querer muito* (to want much, and to love dearly — *eu te quero muito*) carries the delight without spending another Latin word. The preposition gives way to a direct object, which is grammar (D2). *nimis* is σφόδρα here, so *muito*, as 47:2, 92:5, 96:9 (the *nimis* row). **v2:** the Latinist (minor) asked for the preposition *in* back; the stylist heard *quererá muito* as colloquial ('will want a lot'), and the ambiguity reader heard 'want or demand a lot' as a second reading. Portuguese *querer* cannot take *em*, so the preposition and the verb cannot both stay. Ruled for the stylist's *se comprazerá* (free in the psalter; *complacére* is *agradar* / *achar prazer*): it says what *velle in* says here (θέλειν ἐν, DRB 'delight'), keeps *in mandátis* first as the Latin has it, and keeps *nimis* as *muito*. Cost: the *velle* row's verb is not heard; a local rendering for the Hebraism *velle in*, proposed as a glossary row.

options.label: nos seus mandamentos muito se comprazerá

forms.volet: nos seus mandamentos muito se comprazerá

options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's words; the preposition kept, as the Latinist asked.

options.label: quererá muito os seus mandamentos
options.note: Draft 1: the *velle* row, the preposition turned into a direct object; heard as colloquial.

options.label: terá muito prazer nos seus mandamentos

forms.volet: terá muito prazer nos seus mandamentos

options.note: DRB 'delight'; keeps the preposition, but *prazer* is a noun the Latin does not have and spends the word for *voluptas*.

options.label: porá nos seus mandamentos toda a sua vontade

forms.volet: porá nos seus mandamentos toda a sua vontade

options.note: An echo of Ps 1:2 *a sua vontade está na lei do Senhor* (*volúntas*, the same root); refused: a verb and *toda* supplied, and *nimis* is lost in *toda*.

options.label: quererá sem medida os seus mandamentos

forms.volet: quererá sem medida os seus mandamentos

options.note: The *nimis* row's other rendering (118:138, 45:2); kept for *nimis* where it is not σφόδρα.

options.label: nos seus mandamentos quererá muito
options.note: The Latinist's fix; refused — *querer* has no object here and *quererá muito* alone is 'will want a lot'.

decisions.why: *benedícere* God → man is the open row (*bendizer*, Ps 133 and 5:12b). The passive is the easiest place for it: *bendita* is the participle every Brazilian knows from the Ave Maria, and 9:24 *iníquus benedícitur → o iníquo é bendito* is already standing. The CNBB Liturgia das Horas (from the Hebrew; fetched, `consult/lh-ps111-liturgiadashoras-online.html`) sings *abençoada a geração dos homens retos*, and 36:26 has *será abençoada* — but there the Latin is another phrase (*in benedictióne erit*).

options.label: será bendita
options.note: Ruling: the *benedícere* row, as 9:24.

options.label: será abençoada
options.note: MS1932 has *bendita*; *abençoada* is the Brazilian LH's and DM1962's word, and 36:26's (another Latin).

decisions.latin: Glória, et divítiæ in domo ejus
decisions.why: The Latin has no verb; Portuguese needs one (D2). *estão* keeps the Latin's order, so that the colon opens on *Glória* beside the Latin column; *Há* (MS1932, and the Brazilian LH, fetched) is the commoner build but moves the house up. *divítiæ* is plural → *riquezas*, as 36:16, 48:7, 51:9.

options.label: Glória e riquezas estão
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order, a copula supplied.

options.label: Há glória e riquezas
options.note: MS1932 (*Há glória e riqueza na sua casa*).

decisions.latin: Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis
decisions.why: ἐξανέτειλεν: light rising, as the sun rises. The *oríri* row says *nascer*, and the nearest line in the psalter is 96:11 *Lux orta est justo → A luz nasceu para o justo* (ἀνέτειλεν); *exoríri* is the same verb with a prefix. The line is also the Transfiguration versicle (Sancti/08-06, *lumen rectis corde*). 91:8 *exórti fúerint peccatóres sicut fænum → brotarem* is plants, not light. The article: *a luz* as 96:11; *uma luz* (MS1932) is equally faithful — the Latin has none.

options.label: Nasceu … a luz
options.note: Ruling: the *oríri* row and 96:11.

options.label: Nasceu … uma luz
options.note: MS1932's article (*surgiu uma luz*).

options.label: Surgiu … uma luz
options.note: MS1932 word for word; *surgir* is the *oríri* row's option.

options.label: Brotou … a luz
options.note: 91:8's *exoríri* of plants; refused for light.

decisions.why: The Latin names no subject. In the Hebrew acrostic the man is meant; in Ps 110:4 the same two words are said of the Lord, and the Fathers read this line of Christ, the light risen in darkness. MS1932 supplies *ele é*, which still leaves open who *ele* is, but makes a sentence of what the Latin leaves as a cry of attributes. Kept bare, with the Latin's three *et* (a repetition, D2). *miséricors → misericordioso*, *miserátor → compassivo*: the pair row (85:15, 102:8), here in this Latin's order.

options.label: misericordioso, e compassivo, e justo
options.note: Ruling: no subject, as the Latin.

options.label: ele é misericordioso, e compassivo, e justo

forms.miser: ele é misericordioso, e compassivo, e justo

options.note: MS1932 (*ele é misericordioso, compassivo e justo*); DRB *he is*.

options.label: misericordioso, compassivo e justo
options.note: The plain list; drops the Latin's first *et*.

decisions.why: The *jucúndus* row is *agradável* (118:39, 80:3), and this verse is on its list. χρηστός is 'good, kind'; DRB 'acceptable'; MS1932 *Ditoso*, which makes it a second *beátus*. The line answers 111:1 (*Beátus vir … Jucúndus homo*), and *vir / homo* are kept apart as the Latin keeps them (*homem* both: Portuguese has one word). *é* supplied (D2). **v2:** the stylist called *Agradável* the vocabulary of small talk (worst line) and the ambiguity reader heard 'pleasant, likeable'. The row's other places are things (judgments, a psaltery, a word); here it is a man, and χρηστός is 'kind'. *Amável* (the stylist's) is free — *amábilis* never occurs in the psalter (grep) — and says kindness in a person. A local split proposed for the row: *agradável* of things, *amável* of persons.

options.label: Amável é
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's; χρηστός.

options.label: Agradável é
options.note: Draft 1: the row; heard as small talk.

options.label: Bom é
options.note: χρηστός; but *bom* is *bonus*'s word.

options.label: Ditoso
options.note: MS1932; refused — a synonym of *bem-aventurado*, which the Latin does not say, and a word the ear finds old.

decisions.why: *in judício* can be 'with discretion' (DRB 'with judgment', MS1932 *com juízo*) or 'at the judgment / in court' (ἐν κρίσει). Ps 1:5 has the same two words (*non resúrgent ímpii in judício → no juízo*), and the next colon (*in ætérnum non commovébitur*) and 111:7a (*in memória ætérna*) look to the end. *no juízo* keeps the Latin's word and both hearings of a court; *com juízo* chooses prudence. *sermónes → palavras* (D15).

options.label: no juízo
options.note: Ruling: as 1:5.

options.label: com juízo
options.note: MS1932; DRB 'with judgment' — the sense of discretion only.

decisions.why: The formula row *non (com)movébitur in ætérnum* (14:5b, 29:7; 124:1 and this verse listed): *para sempre não será abalado*. Here the Latin itself puts *in ætérnum* before the negation, so the row's order is the Latin's. Two stylists (Pss 14, 29) refused the build and asked *jamais*, which drops *in ætérnum*'s word (D23); the row still waits for a ruling. Followed. **v2:** the third stylist to refuse the build (after Pss 14, 29); the ambiguity reader heard *never* but noted the other parse. Held for the row, which only the main session can rule; the refusal is reported there.

options.label: para sempre não será abalado
options.note: Ruling: the formula row, as 14:5b.

options.label: jamais será abalado
options.note: The Pss 14 and 29 stylists' request.

decisions.why: Lewis & Short give *audítio* as 'a report, hearsay, news' and cite this verse there; ἀκοή. The *timére a* + ablative row makes the thing feared a direct object (90:5). The Latin's order (*ab auditióne mala* first) would give *De notícia má não terá medo*, stilted; natural order under D2. MS1932 *não temerá ouvir notícias funestas* adds a verb and colours the adjective. **v2:** the stylist asked for *a má notícia* (the adjective's natural place, and no final monosyllable). Order and article are grammar (D2), and with *temer* the article is heard as generic. Taken.

options.label: a má notícia
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's order; the article generic after *temer*.

options.label: notícia má
options.note: Draft 1: no article, as the Latin; the adjective after the noun sounds unnatural.

options.label: o mau rumor
options.note: 'Hearsay'; *rumor* is heard as gossip.

decisions.latin: Parátum cor ejus … confirmátum est cor ejus
decisions.why: *parátus* → *pronto* (the row; 56:8 = 107:2 *O meu coração está pronto*). *confirmátum est* (ἐστήρικται): the *confirmáre* row gives *firmar* with persons and things set fast (37:3, 40:13, 70:6 *Em vós fui firmado*, the same Greek), and *fortalecer* where a heart is strengthened by food (103:15). Here the heart is set fast, so *firmado*; the Latin's two *cor ejus* both kept, with the copula *está* supplied twice so the two halves stand parallel.

options.label: pronto … firmado
options.note: Ruling: the *parátus* row and 70:6.

options.label: preparado … firmado
options.note: MS1932 has *disposto*; *preparado* is the *parátus* row's option.

options.label: pronto … fortalecido
options.note: MS1932 *Fortalecido está o seu coração*; 103:15's *fortalecer*.

decisions.why: σκόρπισεν, 'scattered' — his goods, like seed; St Paul quotes the line of the sower (2 Cor 9:9, read in the Mass of St Lawrence, missa/Sancti/08-10). The *dispérgere* row has *dispersar* for people and bones (21:15, 58:12, 88:11); in Portuguese *dispersar* is said of a crowd, and with no object *Dispersou* would be heard of people. *Espalhar* is what one does with seed and alms; it is free in the psalter so far (grep of every prayed.vos.json). *Distribuiu* (MS1932) is *distribúere*'s (D43: *partilhar*) and loses the scattering. A local departure from the row, recorded.

options.label: Espalhou
options.note: Ruling: the scattering kept, said as Portuguese says it of things.

options.label: Dispersou
options.note: The *dispérgere* row.

options.label: Distribuiu
options.note: MS1932; explains, and is another Latin verb's.

decisions.why: *chifre* (the *cornu* row, as 88:25 *será exaltado o seu chifre*). *in glória*: 'gloriously' or 'in the glory (to come)'. *em glória* keeps both; *na glória* (MS1932) leans to heaven. **v2:** the stylist asked *e o seu chifre será exaltado na glória*, to soften the horn's cuckold overtone. Refused: the *e* is not in the Latin, and *na glória* narrows *in glória*; the horn stays unexplained as the *cornu* row rules.

options.label: em glória
options.note: Ruling.

decisions.why: *irásci → irar-se* (the row). The future *se irará* is a knot of r's, which the row already met at 79:5 and 84:6 and solved with a copula and participle (*estareis irado*). Here the anger arises, so *ficará irado*.

options.label: ficará irado
options.note: Ruling: 79:5's remedy.

options.label: se irará
options.note: The row's verb as it stands.

decisions.why: *frémere* has the row *bramir* (2:1 *Por que bramiram as nações*), which names this verse as its other place. But the Greek here is βρύξει τοὺς ὀδόντας αὐτοῦ — word for word the Greek of 36:12 (*stridébit … déntibus suis → rangerá os seus dentes*) and 34:16 (*frenduérunt … déntibus suis → rangeram … os seus dentes*), checked in `consult/parallels/ps034.md`, `ps036.md`; 2:1 is ἐφρύαξαν, another verb. D15's test: three Latin verbs over one Greek → one Portuguese. And *bramir com os dentes* is not something a Brazilian can picture. **v2:** the stylist asked to drop *seus* (a possessive with a body part sounds translated). Refused: the Latin has *suis*, and 36:12 (the same Greek) reads *rangerá os seus dentes*.

options.label: rangerá os seus dentes
options.note: Ruling: = 36:12, by the Greek.

options.label: bramirá com os seus dentes
options.note: The *frémere* row (2:1).

options.label: rangerá os dentes
options.note: The stylist's; drops *suis*.

decisions.why: The *tabéscere* row: *definhar* (118:139, 118:158, 38:12b), L&S 'waste, pine away', ἐκτήκω; this verse is on its list. Blind readers have twice not known it, and it stands. MS1932 and the Brazilian LH have *se consumirá / se consome*, which the row keeps for *consúmere*.

options.label: definhará
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: se consumirá
options.note: MS1932; *consúmere*'s word.

decisions.why: Draft 1 ended the mediant and the final on the same stressed future (*definhará … perecerá*) — an accidental rhyme the Latin does not have (*tabéscet … períbit*), a defect by rule 5; the stylist named it. The verb first, as he proposed: order only (D2), and the verse closes on *pecadores*, a paroxytone as the Latin's *períbit*.

options.label: perecerá o desejo dos pecadores
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's order.

options.label: o desejo dos pecadores perecerá
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order; rhymes with *definhará* at the mediant.

decisions.why: The *despícere (enemies)* row: *olhar de cima*, accusative as 117:7. The stylist heard a social sneer and asked *olhe do alto*. Refused: the row keeps the idiom precisely because *despícere* holds both the height and the contempt (L&S; MS1932 *contemple com desprezo*); *do alto* keeps only the height. It is the row's option, and 53:9, 91:12 and 117:7 would move with it. The ambiguity reader heard triumph or contempt — both the Latin's.

options.label: olhe de cima
options.note: Ruling: the row, = 117:7.

options.label: olhe do alto
options.note: The stylist's; the row's option (*viu do alto*, 91:12).

choices.111:1: *Beátus vir → Bem-aventurado o homem* (D19; Ps 1:1's words). *timére → temer* with the Lord as object; the Brazilian LH's *respeita* (fetched) is refused — *temer* is the row, and the psalm's first line is also the Introit and Gradual of the Commons (Latin there *cupit nimis*).
choices.111:2: *semen → descendência* (D32; no plant image in the verse). The whole verse is a versicle of the Commons (*V. Potens in terra erit semen ejus: generátio rectórum benedicétur*, grep in content/do); each colon reads alone. The Latin's order (*Poderosa … será*) kept: it is also natural Portuguese (MS1932 has it). *rectórum → dos retos* (the *rectus* row).
choices.111:3: *manet in sǽculum sǽculi → permanece pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27; *permanére* row). **The second colon is word for word 110:3b and 111:9b**: the Portuguese is identical in both verses here and in Ps 110:3b, checked against ps110/prayed.vos.json once it was finished (identical). 111:4b's pair matches 110:4 *misericordioso e compassivo*, each in its own Latin's order.
choices.111:4: Also a versicle of the Transfiguration (horas/Sancti/08-06), with *rectis corde*; this colon ends at *retos*, as the psalm does.
choices.111:5: *miserétur et cómmodat → tem piedade e empresta* — copied from 36:26 (the *mutuári / commodáre* row names this verse). The DO verse joins 111:5 and 111:6; the inline (6) is not reproduced. The ambiguity reader heard *no juízo* as the court or the Last Judgment, meaning unclear — the Latin's own range (decision `judicio`); *tem piedade* was heard as compassion first, as in 36:26.
choices.111:7a: The versicle of confessors and the Commons (C4, C9: *V. In memória ætérna erit justus. R. Ab auditióne mala non timébit.*); each colon reads alone. *memória ætérna → memória eterna*: the adjective, not D23's adverbial phrase. *estará* supplied for *erit* (the 'be in' of a place).
choices.111:7b: *despíciat inimícos suos → olhe de cima os seus inimigos*: the *despícere (enemies)* row, accusative as 117:7 (*olharei de cima os meus inimigos*). *non commovébitur → não será abalado* (the *movéri* row). The Latin follows here the Gallican *non commovébitur* where the Greek has οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ; the Latin is followed (rule 1).
choices.111:9: *justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi*: = 111:3b, identical. The first colon is 2 Cor 9:9 and a versicle of St Lawrence (08-10). *paupéribus → aos pobres* (D38 row). The ambiguity reader could not hear what was scattered, nor for certain who scattered it: neither can the Latin (*Dispérsit* has no object and no subject named). The horn was heard with its cuckold overtone, as in Pss 74 and 91; kept by the *cornu* row.
choices.111:10: *desidérium → desejo* (37:10, 77:29); *períre → perecer*. *definhará* was unknown to the ambiguity reader again (the *tabéscere* row; kept).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps111.md (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Read AGENT-BRIEF, DECISIONS (D1–D44), the glossary rows for every word of the psalm, Ps 1 (vos), and the finished lines that share Latin: 36:12, 36:26, 34:16, 96:11, 102:8, 85:15, 88:25, 117:7, 14:5b, 56:8, 70:6, 9:24. Liturgical circulation checked in content/do (grep): 111:1 (Commons, Introit/Gradual, with *cupit*), 111:2 and 111:7a (versicles of the Commons), 111:4 (Transfiguration, *rectis corde*), 111:9a (St Lawrence; 2 Cor 9:9). The Brazilian LH text (CNBB, from the Hebrew) fetched and kept in consult/lh-ps111-liturgiadashoras-online.html: *Feliz o homem que respeita o Senhor * e que ama com carinho a sua lei*, *abençoada a geração dos homens retos*, *Haverá glória e riqueza em sua casa*, *range os dentes e de inveja se consome* — the wording Brazilians sing at Sunday Vespers; it is Hebrew-family and a witness of circulation only. Ps 110 (the twin, shared *justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi* and *miséricors et miserátor*) had no draft on disk when this was written; the shared colon follows the glossary rows, and Ps 110 should read the same. Hard readings: *volet nimis in* (Hebraism of delight), *in judício* (discretion or judgment), *fremet* (Greek = 36:12's βρύξει), *Dispérsit* (things, not people).

Hard checks pass (ids 111:1–10 with 111:7a/7b; every mark). Soft length flags accepted: 111:1a +5 (*Bem-aventurado o homem*, D19, as 1:1); 111:2a +5 (*descendência*, D32); 111:3b and 111:9b +4 (*pelos séculos dos séculos*, D27); 111:4b +3 (the Latin's three *et* kept); 111:5a +4 (*é* supplied, *tem piedade* = 36:26); 111:7a second colon −4 (*não temerá notícia má*: the Latin's four words, nothing to add); 111:7b first colon +4 and third +3 (the two *o seu coração está* kept parallel; *olhar de cima* is the row). Cadences: oxytone endings (*Senhor*, *má*, *definhará*, *perecerá*) are allowed by rule 4.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, Portuguese only. 23 ambiguities, nearly all the Latin's own (whose house, whose justice, who is *misericordioso*, what was scattered); two acted on through the stylist's fixes (*Agradável*, *quererá muito*). Unknown words: *definhará*, *retos* — both glossary rows, kept.

outcomes.remark: 'quererá muito' heard as wanting / demanding a lot
'no juízo' heard as court / Last Judgment, meaning unclear
outcomes.reason: The Latin's *in judício* (as 1:5) holds the court and the judgment; *com juízo* stays the option.
The Latin names no subject; kept open on purpose.

The *tabéscere* row; unknown to earlier readers too, and it stands there.

audit.note: v2: 111:1 *nos seus mandamentos muito se comprazerá* (Latinist + stylist); 111:5 *Amável é o homem* (stylist, a local split of the *jucúndus* row for persons); 111:7a *a má notícia* (order); 111:10 *perecerá o desejo dos pecadores* (order, to break the *-rá* rhyme at mediant and final). New decisions `despiciat` and `v10c` hold the refused and the draft wordings. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.

v2: hard checks pass. New soft flags accepted: 111:1b +4 (*se comprazerá* for *volet*, the preposition kept); 111:5a now +3 (*Amável*), 111:7a second colon −3 (was −4). 111:10 final now paroxytone, no -rá rhyme with the mediant.
